hypothesis: The 1.4 Extract handler aborts at a pre-ctor exit block (the ctor is never reached)
test: Breakpoint at EXTRACT_CTOR (base+0x1a44220) during a live Extract with a valid free pad
notes: QEMU gdbstub hit the ctor: PC 0xaaaaac4e4220, thread p01.01; the app then entered Saving changes

hypothesis: The handler abort is the pad lookup: a nulled slot has no pad object, whereas a non-null but non-busy pad passes
test: Empty pad 0 layer vector (end=begin) so PAD_BUSY is false while the slot stays non-null, then run the Extract
notes: FREE_PAD returned Some(0) and the slot stayed a live Instrument; the pad lookup was not the sole blocker

hypothesis: Exit trampolines can record the handler's failing gate
test: In-process trampolines on the exit blocks record the hit address during a live Extract
notes: The trampolines crashed (stub outside the b range; ADRP exits cannot be copied). The QEMU gdbstub replaced them and works

hypothesis: With a valid free pad the handler reaches the ctor and only the SDK arming fails
test: Write /run/ctor_diag from ctor_entry and run Generated with a valid free pad
notes: The diag-based test was invalid: the gdbstub proved the ctor IS reached. Whether the hook armed and whether EXTRACT_EXEC ran is still open (see PORTING-TO-1_4.md sections 6.3 and 7.2)

hypothesis: The generated Extract returns NotApplied because the destination instrument remains the same while its sample changes
test: Run current SDK on 1.4 with a live source and valid free instrument; record result and destination sample before and after
notes: Live probe returned Ok and sample pointer changed, but the instrument layer vector remained empty; assignment and playback are not established. Artificial emptying leaves a stale layer pointer.

hypothesis: An empty layer vector must not count its stale sample pointer as an assignment
test: Require a nonempty layer vector, then repeat using a pad cleared by the app
notes: The artificial empty-vector probe returned Ok with the sample beyond the vector end. The regression rejects it; a pad cleared through the app has a live layer and Extract returns Ok with 44100 frames.

hypothesis: The native writer uses the source sample channel count regardless of the supplied rendered buffer channel count, causing an overread for mono input on a stereo seed
test: Compare the generated mono input to the stereo WAV saved by the app and inspect samples beyond the input allocation
notes: The stereo WAV starts with consecutive mono samples in alternating channels and its second half contains unrelated values and NaNs; the source seed reports two channels.

hypothesis: The 1.4 slice selection and chop predicate work when the chop view is actually active
test: Activate CHOP on a selected sample and call write_markers while logging chop mode, connector values, and resulting slices
notes: On the visible CHOP screen write_markers returned true and the four markers appeared, but chop_mode and event.chop_mode were false. Connector +0x618 is a pointer, so the selection target remains unverified.

hypothesis: The 1.4 DATA target is the embedded object at button surface +0x2da8
test: Compare button and DATA encoder event addresses during a real panel turn
notes: Button surface 0xffffe3fef870; DATA encoder 0xffffe3ff2618; difference 0x2da8. Pad pressure uses a separate surface object.

hypothesis: The CHOP flag is bit 0 at the page controller +0x53
test: Toggle CHOP off/on/off and compare flag and SDK paint event
notes: Flag and updated chop_mode were false/true/false with the displayed modes.

hypothesis: The selection setter targets the model at the 1.4 layer connector +0x618
test: Replace four slices, select slice 3, replace again, and observe settled selection
notes: Native handler uses connector +0x618; the live selection changed from index 2 to index 0 after the asynchronous update.
